item.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
item.description: A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.
item.content:encoded:
A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.

(Image credit: Dillon J. Amaya)

item.title: Those lake "weeds" actually keep lakes healthy
item.description: Some people may think that plants that grow in lakes are weeds that should be removed, but ecologists say native aquatic plants keep lakes healthy. They also prevent invasive species from taking over.
item.content:encoded: Some people may think that plants that grow in lakes are weeds that should be removed, but ecologists say native aquatic plants keep lakes healthy. They also prevent invasive species from taking over.

item.title: Group that plants fruit trees in vacant lots grows to cities nationwide
item.description: A Kansas City group set up to help volunteers plant fruit trees in vacant city lots has quickly branched out across the country with almost 850 orchards in 17 cities with more to come.

item.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
item.description: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.

item.title: Navajo environmentalists were offered money to drop opposition to energy project
item.description: On the Navajo Reservation, a would-be energy developer appears to have tried to bribe a local environmental group to drop opposition to his project.

item.title: Isaias pummels the Gulf Coast, and plows through Alabama
item.description: Hurricane Isaias landed Friday night on the Florida Gulf Coast. The storm was expected to bring life-threatening storm surge, damaging winds, flooding and the possibility of tornados.

item.title: Wildfire smoke affects animals in unique ways. Scientists are trying to understand it
item.description: The new field of "smoke ecology" examines how wildfire smoke perturbs wild places and animals — and what might be done to prevent its worst mayhem.

item.description: Oct. 1 is when new federal rules for sharing the Colorado River start. It's going to be messy and courts will likely have to weigh in.

item.description: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah to power a huge data center project.

item.title: The race to protect Santa Rosa Island's rare, damaged Torrey pines
item.description: In May, a fire damaged 80% of the trees one of the only two naturally-occurring groves of Torrey Pines in the world. The National Park Service is trying to help them recover.
